text:
anya: Hey team — first week here! I got a company Windows 11 laptop and I'm trying to get the dev environment up. Hitting a few snags: WSL2 install hangs, Docker Desktop can't start (VM/Hyper-V errors), and asdf/node setup seems to fail behind our proxy. Also need to get GPG commit signing and access to env vars in 1Password. Any quick checklist?

sam: welcome anya :wave: 1) WSL2 + Docker Desktop are the usual blockers on corp images. Did IT enable Virtualization and Hyper-V?

anya: I think virtualization is enabled in BIOS but Hyper-V isn't. Tried `wsl --install` and it stalled at the kernel update step.

it-bot: Laptop enrollment complete. Endpoint security (CrowdSec) is enforcing outbound proxy at 10.0.5.2:3128. If you need exceptions, ping IT.

devontae: if proxy is blocking kernel update, download the WSL2 kernel MSI directly and install offline: https://aka.ms/wsl2kernel. Then run `wsl --set-default-version 2`. For Hyper-V, run PowerShell as admin: `dism.exe /online /enable-feature /featurename:Microsoft-Hyper-V /all` and reboot.

ben: For Docker Desktop: make sure WSL integration is enabled and that Docker uses WSL backend (not Hyper-V). Settings -> General -> Use the WSL 2 based engine. If Docker Desktop refuses to start after corp AV, try adding Docker Desktop to exclusions or ask infra to allow virtualization for the installer.

maya: proxy + npm/asdf tips: set proxy envs in both Windows and WSL. In PowerShell: `setx HTTP_PROXY "http://10.0.5.2:3128"` and inside WSL: `export http_proxy=http://10.0.5.2:3128` in your `~/.profile`. For asdf plugin installs that call out to GitHub, use `GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY=1 git clone ...` as a temporary fallback (ask security first).

anya: thanks — any specific commands for asdf/node and the internal npm registry?

devontae: sequence I used on Windows+WSL:
```
# inside WSL distro (ubuntu)
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y curl git build-essential libssl-dev
git clone https://github.com/asdf-vm/asdf.git ~/.asdf --branch v0.12.0
. "$HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh"
asdf plugin-add nodejs
asdf install nodejs 18.17.1
asdf global nodejs 18.17.1
```
Then add the internal registry and auth in your WSL home `~/.npmrc`:
```
registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
@redwood:registry=https://npm.pkg.redwood.internal/
//npm.pkg.redwood.internal/:_authToken=${REDWOOD_NPM_TOKEN}
```
Use the CLI to fetch the token (see below).

ben: to pull secrets we use 1Password CLI. After installing `op` in WSL, run `eval $(op signin redwood)` then `op item get "dev/redwood/npm-token" --fields label=token` and export to `REDWOOD_NPM_TOKEN`. We keep detailed steps in onboarding docs but you can also run `rwd login` (internal CLI) to populate `~/.redwood/credentials`.

anya: GPG for commit signing? I haven't set that up before.

maya: I do commit signing in WSL. Quick steps:
```
# generate
gpg --full-generate-key
# list
gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format LONG
# configure git (replace KEYID)
git config --global user.signingkey KEYID
git config --global commit.gpgsign true
```
If Windows Git (VSCode) won't pick up the WSL gpg agent, use `gpg-wsl` or configure `gpg` as a ssh-agent forward. We have a docs page: https://internal.redwood.ai/dev/git-gpg#wsl

sam: FYI our devcontainer templates expect docker & WSL working. Once Docker is sane, open repo in VS Code and run 'Rebuild Container' from the Command Palette. If you get permission errors, run Docker Desktop once as admin.

anya: a couple errors I hit while following these: `EACCES: permission denied` when asdf tried to write to `~/.asdf`, and `op: command not found` after signing in.

devontae: for permission denied, make sure your WSL home is owned by you: `sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) $HOME`. For `op`, install the 1Password CLI inside WSL (not Windows): `curl -sS https://downloads.1password.com/linux/static/1password-cli/2.9.0/op_linux_amd64_v2.9.0.zip -o op.zip` then unzip and move to `/usr/local/bin/op`. Or use the distro package if available.

ben: also check that your VSCode Remote - WSL extension is up-to-date. If `op` is still missing in container, add it to the devcontainer Dockerfile so the container can fetch secrets at build time (we add `op` + `awscli` to most devcontainers).

maya: small gotcha: company SSO MFA popup sometimes opens the Windows browser and the WSL `op signin` fails because callbacks can't reach WSL. Workaround: run `op signin --raw` in Windows PowerShell, copy the token into WSL env var `OP_SESSION_redwood` before running `op item get`.

anya: this is gold, thanks. Last Q: how do I get the `rwd` internal CLI?

sam: `curl -fsSL https://internal.redwood.ai/cli/install.sh | bash` or via brew on Mac, but for WSL we have a package in our apt repo; add the repo with `curl https://internal.redwood.ai/repos/deb/setup.sh | sudo bash` then `sudo apt install rwd-cli`. If you prefer, I'll add you to the beta group so you can `rwd login` and get tokens automatically.

anya: please add me to the beta group @sam, and @it-bot if there's any laptop exemption request.

it-bot: IT ticket created #IT-4621 for virtualization/installer exemptions. Assigned to infra-team.

maya: ping if you want a quick pair session — I can remote in and help finish the WSL/Docker bits.

anya: will do — thanks everyone :heart:
